title: Start X
subtitle: startx → TinyX → framebuffer + input UAPI
what_you_see: A gray root window (historic capture) or twm + xterm after startx on a writable HOME. Pointer and keyboard move the session.
why_it_matters: IR0 does not fork TinyX. The kernel must expose Linux-compatible /dev/fb0, socket, poll, and input read semantics so unmodified KDrive/TinyX runs. Real third-party software found a read(2) contract bug — fixed in kernel input, not in X.

dual_view.user:
ivan@ir0:~$ startx
( gray root window / twm appears )
dual_view.kernel:
startx → xinit
  ↓ TinyX opens /dev/fb0 mmap
  ↓ unix socket + poll
  ↓ read(/dev/events0 or mouse)
  ↓ must respect count byte!

steps.label: startx
steps.what_ir0_does: Shell script launches xinit, which execs the X server and window manager.
steps.why_it_matters: All policy is userspace — kernel only provides devices and syscalls.

steps.label: exec X server
steps.what_ir0_does: TinyX/KDrive binary loaded like any ELF. No IR0-specific patches in upstream X.
steps.why_it_matters: Compatibility strategy: kernel adapts, userspace stays stock.

steps.label: /dev/fb0
steps.what_ir0_does: mmap MAP_SHARED of framebuffer memory. Console may hand off to fb backend.
steps.why_it_matters: Tier-2 graphics clients depend on fb UAPI parity.

steps.label: Input devices
steps.what_ir0_does: X reads events with read(2). IR0 must not return more bytes than requested — a real bug found by running unmodified TinyX.
steps.why_it_matters: Contract violations surface only under real software.

steps.label: TinyX root window
steps.what_ir0_does: Server draws root window, accepts clients. Historic gray capture documents first success.
steps.why_it_matters: Pedagogically honest milestone — not replaced by a mock polished desktop.
